dossier.valuation_method: Probability-weighted composite (net-cash/NAV asset value + discrete optionality scenarios, weights anchored to the 2020-22 space-SPAC cohort base rate), cross-checked against net-cash NAV; minority/status-quo value (headline ~$1.33) separated from control/takeover value (~$1.55-1.60). DCF and trailing/forward multiples rejected as primary methods for a pre-commercial, negative-gross-margin serial diluter.
dossier.thesis_summary: Sidus is a pre-commercial space-and-defense micro-cap best valued as a ~$165M just-raised cash pile (~$1.60/share net cash) attached to a value-destroying operation (-168% gross margin, revenue down four straight years, ~47% related-party) plus genuine but low-probability defense/data optionality. Because the operation in expectation burns the cash faster than the optionality creates value, and the CEO's super-voting control prevents minority holders from forcing a payout, the probability-weighted minority FMV (~$1.33) sits BELOW net cash; a control buyer who halted the burn could capture closer to net cash (~$1.55-1.60). Scenario weights are anchored to a cohort base rate where only ~15% of such companies reach durable positive gross margin; Sidus has already executed a 1-for-100 reverse split.
key_value_drivers: Pro-forma net cash ~$165M after April ($58.5M) and May ($100M) 2026 raises vs ~$0.7M debt
Gross margin inflection (currently -168%) - the single decisive variable, and the data/SaaS-vs-manufacturer margin profile that sets the re-rate multiple (3x vs 6-7x)
Conversion of SHIELD/Golden Dome IDIQ into funded task orders
Start and scaling of LizzieSat data subscriptions and Fortis VPX compute revenue
Magnitude/price of future equity dilution (raises above NAV are accretive to cash/share; raises below NAV are destructive)
CEO super-voting control gating any control-value realization
key_risks: Negative gross margin operation consumes cash with no proven path to gross profit
Going-concern dependence on serial equity dilution (post a 1-for-100 reverse split); capital markets are effectively the business model
~47% of revenue is related-party (parent Craig Technical); consolidated VIE (Aurea Alas) adds related-party complexity
Super-voting Class B control by CEO/parent; minority Class A holders cannot force liquidation, making control value unattainable
Commercialization perpetually 'imminent'; no contracted backlog disclosed
Satellites are wasting assets - LS1 already impaired $4.5M and being de-orbited
what_would_change_my_mind: Two+ consecutive quarters of positive gross margin with growing third-party revenue
A disclosed contracted backlog underwriting forward revenue
A funded SHIELD/Golden Dome task order of scale
Evidence the company can reach breakeven without further dilution (cash becomes a true floor)
A friendly strategic sale near/above net cash
Conversely: burn accelerating beyond ~$40M/yr with falling revenue, or a distressed/reverse-split raise
